title: Animal Spirits
gist: Jackson Lears traces 'animal spirits' from early-modern medicine through Keynes to argue that vitalism—spontaneity, play, irreducible life force—is a suppressed counter-current to utilitarian, rational-actor modernity. He argues technocratic neoliberalism's denial of these needs fuels populist backlash (Trump 2016) and that Keynes's animal spirits are a better model of investment than Schumpeterian creative destruction or rational choice.

insights.claim: Keynes held that most investment decisions stem from 'animal spirits'—a spontaneous urge to action—rather than exact calculation of future benefits, challenging the rational self-interested actor at the core of market utilitarian thought.
insights.speaker: https://hedgehogreview.com/contributors/jackson-lears
insights.so_what: Investment cycles are driven by sentiment/confidence regimes, not just expected-return math.
insights.quote: Keynes argued that most investment decisions were “a result of animal spirits—of a spontaneous urge to action rather than inaction,” rather than “an exact calculation of benefits to come.”
insights.locator: Intellectual obituaries are a risky business.

insights.claim: Lears argues Keynes was psychologically more sophisticated than Schumpeter, whose 'creative destruction' has become a capitalist providentialism assuming innovation will always make things work out regardless of hollowed-out cities or squandered resources.

themes.theme: Money as imagined value and the confidence man

insights.claim: The rise of a stable, bounded model of the self (Adam Smith, Scottish common sense) coincided with paper money, when property became effectively imaginary and its value depended on investors' fluctuating feelings of trust, doubt or panic.
insights.speaker: https://hedgehogreview.com/contributors/jackson-lears
insights.so_what: Fiat/financial assets are confidence instruments; narratives of stability are ballast for inherently sentiment-driven values.
insights.quote: Money was a sign, not a thing; its meaning was increasingly related to the mingled feelings it evoked—trust or mistrust, confidence or doubt or even panic.

insights.claim: The self-made man and the confidence man are paired ideal types in market society: the sincere self-made man exists culturally to stabilize the shape-shifting, bubble-blowing confidence man, who needs animal spirits to keep his entrepreneurial energy going.
